title: AI 数据中心遭反对潮，硅谷巨头砸钱"灭火"
content:
According to the Wall Street Journal, U.S. tech companies are seeking public support for data center construction through open days, job commitments, and large sums of money. In July, around a thousand residents in Georgia gathered, holding signs with slogans such as "I didn't vote for AI" and "Data can't be drunk," to attend an informational session on OpenAI's proposed data center—on-site there were also tacos and up to $71 million in programming learning credits, along with a commitment to invest $80 million in the community.
From Secrecy to "Incentive" Campaigns
Previously, the industry relied on fast-tracking, secret operations, and political connections to secure land, but now grassroots opposition is threatening the foundation of AI prosperity: multiple projects have been derailed, and political allies have withdrawn. Tech giants have fully shifted to a "fire-fighting" approach, adding job guarantees, investments in clean water, and promoting that data centers can reduce residents' tax burdens; Meta established a $1 billion community fund, and Zuckerberg wrote a 6,500-word article stating that the Hyperion project brought teachers in the area up to $50,000 in bonuses, and promised to achieve "water resource positive impact" by 2030.
Data centers have become the most prominent political issue: Gallup shows that 71% of Americans oppose building them locally, and the number of projects blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 has reached a record high. New York State has temporarily banned large-scale construction, and Pennsylvania has imposed strict regulations. After the last election, Microsoft realized the issue was decisive and thus stopped signing community confidentiality agreements and introduced a package of commitments on power, water, jobs, and taxes; Amazon and others also signed the White House "Taxpayer Protection Pledge," taking on electricity costs without passing them on to consumers.
However, academia warns that there is a gap between public relations rhetoric and actual actions—one side says they are good neighbors, while the other opposes the suspension of construction laws. Microsoft's president Smith also admitted that without substantial promotional activities, the effect is limited, "people are smart and will find information themselves." Whether this "fire-fighting" effort will work still depends on whether the giants can implement their promises effectively in practice.

report.summary: 硅谷巨头用开放日、资金和承诺应对AI数据中心选址引发的民众反对潮。
report.background: 随着AI算力需求暴增，科技巨头加速建设数据中心，但选址常引起当地居民对水电消耗、环境噪音和生活成本的担忧。此前行业常靠保密和政商关系快速拿地，如今草根反对力量增强，项目频繁受阻。为扭转舆论，OpenAI、Meta、微软等转向公开宣传和利益输送，试图用社区投资、就业承诺和环保目标换取支持。
key_points: OpenAI在佐治亚州举办开放日活动，发放免费塔可并承诺7100万美元编程学习积分和8000万美元社区投资，以争取当地居民支持。
Meta设立10亿美元社区基金，扎克伯格发文称其Hyperion项目为当地教师带来高额奖金，并承诺2030年前实现‘水资源正效益’。
民调显示71%美国人反对在本地建数据中心，2026年第一季度被阻挠或延迟的项目数量创历史新高，纽约州和宾州已收紧监管。
微软放弃保密协议，转向承诺电力、水源、就业和税收方面的保障；亚马逊等公司签署白宫‘纳税人保护承诺’，避免电费转嫁消费者。
学术界质疑宣传与实际行动存在差距，微软总裁也承认纯公关效果有限，民众会自行查证信息。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，数据中心选址成本和法律风险显著上升，企业需将社区关系纳入战略规划。对开发者来说，算力供给可能因项目延迟而趋紧，影响模型训练和部署。对普通用户，社区承诺有望改善基础设施和公共服务，但也需警惕企业承诺落空，以及数据中心带来的环境与生活影响。
report.tools: 关注数据中心合规与社区沟通策略，可参考Microsoft的社区承诺框架、Meta的Hyperion项目公开报告；若想追踪数据中心的能源与环境数据，可关注Green Software Foundation的SCI标准，以及数据中心行业开放数据平台如DC Byte。
